rootCauseHypothesis.evidence: The portrait trace's first runway contact is an early tip contact around x=301.95 with contact point x≈338.845 and normal (0,-1); the existing suppression begins at x>=350. Threshold-only suppression at 250 and 290 was rejected because it broke the fixed forward replay.
rootCauseHypothesis.changeHypothesis: For level1-runway-main only, route an approaching sharp top-face contact (normalY <= -0.9 and velocity into the surface) through the existing respondToHardSurface recovery response instead of anchoring. Keep the x>=350 suppression, opening white-landing behavior, blunt body/handle branch, and debug fixture bypass unchanged.
rejectedAlternatives: x>=250 threshold-only sharp suppression: focused assertion passed but seed-31 forward replay ended at 4.575 seconds before runway traversal.
x>=290 threshold-only sharp suppression: replay fell at about x=967.47 and 5.392 seconds before the stack.
Broad runway removal or renderer-only masking: conflicts with the authored visible support and prior collision evidence.

The focused test proves the response remains forward-moving or upward-recovering with anchorId null after the early contact.
An early sharp runway contact with a non-top normal retains its authored anchor behavior.
The later x>=350 sharp runway behavior remains airborne and the runway body/handle contact still emits a controlled bounce.
The opening white-landing teaching anchor remains the first authored opening anchor.
The seed-31 fixed timestamp replay reaches at least 11.9 seconds and player x>2000 without failing.
Only the two owned source/test files change; no debug fixture or renderer path is altered.
pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck pass and exactly one pnpm build succeeds with a recorded dist hash.
The Fixer receipt makes no natural or perceptual QA claim; independent Playwright QA must retest portrait and desktop normal input.
